veg.n: Frat house sticky barbecue tofu wings
veg.make_ahead: Press and tear the tofu up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; make the glaze up to 3 days ahead. Bake and glaze on the night.

steps.text: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and press it under a heavy pan for 15 minutes, then tear it into 4 cm chunks.
Toss the tofu with the cornflour, paprika, olive oil and salt until every piece is coated.
Spread the tofu on two lined trays and bake at 220C for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Simmer the barbecue sauce with the honey, soy and cider vinegar for 5 minutes until sticky.
Toss the hot tofu in the glaze and return to the oven for 5 minutes to caramelise.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onions.

veg.make_ahead: Make the blue cheese dip up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; tear the mushrooms and cut the celery up to 1 day ahead. Roast and toss just before serving.

steps.text: Tear the oyster mushrooms into thick clusters and toss with the cornflour, olive oil and salt.
Roast on a lined tray at 220C for 22 minutes, turning once, until golden with crisp edges.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the mushrooms through it.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream for the dip. Serve with the celery sticks.

veg.n: King oyster of the Cave wings
veg.make_ahead: Shred the king oyster mushrooms up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge; make the honey sriracha glaze up to 3 days ahead. Batter and fry on the night.

steps.text: Halve the king oyster mushrooms lengthways and shred them with a fork into thick strips.
Whisk the flour, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt with the cold water into a thick batter.
Heat the vegetable oil to 175C in a deep heavy pot.
Dip the mushroom strips in the batter and fry in batches for 5 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
Simmer the honey, sriracha and soy for 4 minutes until glossy and toss the fried mushrooms through.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the cauliflower into florets and make the blue cheese dip up to 1 day ahead and keep both chilled. Batter, bake and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the cauliflower into large florets.
Whisk the flour, water, garlic powder and salt into a smooth batter and coat each floret.
Bake on a lined tray at 220C for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the florets through.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream and serve with the celery sticks.

veg.n: Aunt Cass's hot gochujang tempeh wings
veg.make_ahead: Simmer and cut the tempeh up to 1 day ahead and keep it chilled; make the gochujang glaze up to 3 days ahead. Bake and glaze on the night.

steps.text: Cut the tempeh into thick fingers and simmer in a pot of water for 10 minutes to soften, then drain well.
Toss the tempeh with the vegetable oil and salt.
Bake at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp and browned.
Warm the gochujang with the honey, garlic and soy for 3 minutes until glossy.
Toss the tempeh through the glaze and scatter with the sesame seeds.

veg.n: Dr Farthing's gambling debt buffalo jackfruit wings
veg.make_ahead: Drain, squeeze and pull the jackfruit up to 1 day ahead and keep it chilled; make the blue cheese dip up to 2 days ahead. Bake and toss on the night.

ingredients.item: tins (400g) young green jackfruit in brine

steps.text: Drain the jackfruit from the brine, rinse well and squeeze out as much water as you can.
Pull the jackfruit apart into shreds, discarding any tough core, then toss with the cornflour, olive oil and salt.
Spread on a lined tray and bake at 220C for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp at the edges.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the jackfruit through it.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream with a squeeze of lemon. Serve the jackfruit hot with the dip and celery.

veg.make_ahead: Cut and dust the haloumi up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; mix the herb sour cream and cut the celery the same day. Fry and toss just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the haloumi into thick fingers, pat dry and dust with the cornflour.
Pan-fry in the olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until deep golden.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and honey and toss the haloumi through.
Stir the chopped herbs through the sour cream and serve with the celery sticks to put the fire out.

veg.n: Hawkmen sky city honey soy eggplant wings
veg.make_ahead: Cut the eggplant up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; make the honey soy glaze up to 3 days ahead. Roast and glaze on the night.

steps.text: Cut the eggplants into 4 cm chunks and toss with the olive oil and salt.
Roast on two trays at 220C for 35 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and soft inside.
Warm the honey, soy and chilli for 3 minutes until sticky.
Toss the eggplant through the glaze and scatter with the sesame seeds.

veg.n: Car wash corner store battered onion wings
veg.make_ahead: Cut the onions into petals up to 1 day ahead and keep them chilled; the ranch can sit in the fridge as well. Batter, fry and toss just before serving.

steps.text: Peel the onions, cut each into 6 wedges and separate into thick petals.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt with the cold water into a thick batter.
Heat the vegetable oil to 180C in a deep heavy pot.
Dip the onion petals in the batter and fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden, then drain.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce, toss the onion through it and serve with the ranch dressing.

veg.make_ahead: Cut and toss the haloumi in the cornflour up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; chop the chillies the same day. Bake and glaze just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the haloumi into bite-sized cubes and toss with the cornflour and olive oil.
Bake at 220C for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Warm the butter with the honey, soy sauce and chopped red chillies until sticky and toss the haloumi through until glossy.

veg.n: Annexation of Puerto Rico barbecue jackfruit wings
veg.make_ahead: Drain, squeeze and pull the jackfruit up to 1 day ahead and keep it chilled; mix the ranch dip up to 2 days ahead. Roast and glaze on the night.

ingredients.item: tins (400g) young green jackfruit in brine

steps.text: Drain the jackfruit from the brine, rinse and squeeze it dry, then pull it into shreds and discard any tough core.
Toss the jackfruit with the olive oil, smoked paprika and salt and roast at 220C for 30 minutes until the edges crisp.
Warm the honey with the barbecue sauce and toss the jackfruit through, then return to the oven for 5 minutes.
Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise and chopped herbs into a ranch dip. Serve with the celery sticks.

veg.make_ahead: Cut and toss the paneer in the cornflour up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Bake and glaze just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the paneer into thick fingers and toss with the cornflour, olive oil and salt.
Bake on a lined tray at 220C for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Melt the butter with the honey, sweet chilli sauce, chilli flakes, lime zest and lime juice.
Toss the paneer through the glaze and scatter with the coriander.

veg.n: Sturdy Wings honey soy tempeh wings
veg.make_ahead: Simmer and cut the tempeh up to 1 day ahead and keep it chilled; make the honey soy glaze up to 3 days ahead. Bake and glaze on the night.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Cut the tempeh into thick fingers, simmer in water for 10 minutes, then drain well.
Toss the tempeh with the vegetable oil and salt and bake on a rack for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Simmer the honey, soy, garlic, ginger and rice vinegar for 3 minutes until syrupy.
Toss the tempeh in the glaze and scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onions.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the cauliflower into florets and mix the ranch dip up to 1 day ahead and keep both chilled. Roast and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the cauliflower into large florets and toss with the olive oil and salt.
Roast on a rack at 220C for 35 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and browned.
Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, chives, garlic powder and lemon juice for the ranch dip.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss through the cauliflower.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the broccoli into florets and slice the spring onions up to 1 day ahead and keep them chilled. Roast and glaze just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into large florets with a little stem on each and toss with the olive oil and salt.
Roast at 220C for 18 minutes, turning once, until charred at the tips.
Melt the chilli sauce, honey and butter and toss the broccoli through.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onions.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the cauliflower into florets and make the blue cheese dip up to 1 day ahead and keep both chilled. Coat, bake and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the cauliflower into large florets and toss with the olive oil, baking powder and salt.
Bake on a rack at 220C for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Mash the blue cheese with the sour cream, mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon for the dip.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the cauliflower through it. Serve with the dip and celery.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the paneer and crush the garlic up to 1 day ahead and keep them chilled. Fry and glaze just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the paneer into thick fingers and toss with the cornflour and salt.
Pan-fry in the olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Melt the butter with the honey, garlic and thyme for 2 minutes.
Toss the hot paneer through the glaze until shiny and golden and serve on a big platter.

veg.make_ahead: Make the blue cheese dip up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; trim the mushrooms and cut the celery up to 1 day ahead. Fry and toss just before serving.

steps.text: Trim the oyster mushrooms into thick clusters.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over high heat, add the mushrooms in batches, press down with a plate and fry for 5 minutes each side until crisp. Season with the salt.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the mushrooms through.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream for a dip and serve with the celery sticks.

veg.make_ahead: Crumb the eggplant up to 1 day ahead and keep it on a tray covered in the fridge; make the blue cheese dip up to 2 days ahead. Bake and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the eggplants into thick fingers and season with the salt.
Coat each finger in the flour, then the beaten eggs, then the panko breadcrumbs.
Drizzle with the olive oil and bake on a lined tray at 220C for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Melt the hot sauce with the butter and honey and toss the eggplant through it.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream. Serve the eggplant with the dip and celery.

veg.make_ahead: Cut the broccoli into florets and make the blue cheese dip up to 1 day ahead and keep both chilled. Batter, bake and toss on the night.

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into large florets.
Whisk the flour, water and salt into a thin batter and coat each floret.
Bake on a lined tray at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss the broccoli through.
Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream for the dip and serve with the celery sticks.
